title: Postgres cluster (Patroni)
description: The Patroni cluster behind Grafana, NetBox and dark-triage: leader and VIP, health checks, members, failovers, replication, the apps' load, WAL archive and backups, etcd and the VMs.

panels.title: Leader
panels.description: The member holding Patroni's leader key: it takes the writes, archives WAL and runs the nightly backup. Click for its instance dashboard.

panels.title: VIP on
panels.description: The member that holds the keepalived VIP (10.13.11.104, what Grafana, NetBox and dark-triage connect to). keepalived checks Patroni's /primary, so it must be the leader.

panels.title: Checks
panels.description: The cluster's invariants, the same ones the postgres alert group watches: one leader with the VIP, every replica streaming and within maximum_lag_on_failover (1 MiB, else it can't take over), Patroni not paused, etcd quorum (2 of 3), WAL reaching S3 (archive_timeout 300 s), a full backup in the last 36 h (daily at 01:30) and haproxy seeing at least one RGW.

targets.expr: (count(node_network_address_info{job="node", role="postgres", device=~"vrrp.*"} and on (host) (patroni_primary{job="patroni", scope="$scope"} == 1)) or vector(0)) == bool 1

(count(patroni_replica{job="patroni", scope="$scope"} == 1 and on (host) patroni_postgres_streaming{job="patroni", scope="$scope"} == 1) or vector(0)) >= bool (count(patroni_version{job="patroni", scope="$scope"}) - 1)

(max(scalar(max(patroni_xlog_location{job="patroni", scope="$scope"} and on (host) (patroni_primary{job="patroni", scope="$scope"} == 1))) - (patroni_xlog_replayed_location{job="patroni", scope="$scope"} and on (host) (patroni_replica{job="patroni", scope="$scope"} == 1))) or vector(0)) < bool 1048576

panels.title: Timeline
panels.description: Postgres' timeline: +1 at every switchover or failover.

panels.title: Leader changes in range
panels.description: Timeline increments in the time range: planned switchovers and failovers alike. See Failover history.

panels.title: Last full backup
panels.description: Age of the last successful pgBackRest full backup of this stanza (pg-backup.timer on the leader, daily 01:30; alert PostgresBackupTooOld after 36 h).

panels.title: Last WAL archived
panels.description: Since the leader last pushed a WAL segment to S3. With writes it's at most archive_timeout (300 s); with no writes at all it grows (alert PostgresWALArchiveStale at 1 h).

panels.title: Connections used
panels.description: The busiest member's backends against max_connections (200).

panels.title: Leader WAL rate
panels.description: WAL the leader writes per second: the write load all three apps put on the cluster.

panels.title: Members
panels.description: One row per Patroni member. Replay lag: WAL bytes behind the leader (Patroni's view; over 1 MiB it can't be elected). Lag (time): since the last replayed transaction while WAL is pending. DCS seen: since the member last refreshed its key in etcd (Patroni's ttl is 30 s). Slots WAL: WAL the member keeps for replication slots (Patroni keeps slots for every member, on replicas too). Click a member for its instance dashboard.

targets.expr: max by (host) (scalar(max(patroni_xlog_location{job="patroni", scope="$scope"} and on (host) (patroni_primary{job="patroni", scope="$scope"} == 1))) - (patroni_xlog_replayed_location{job="patroni", scope="$scope"} and on (host) (patroni_replica{job="patroni", scope="$scope"} == 1))) or max by (host) (patroni_primary{job="patroni", scope="$scope"} == 1) * 0

panels.title: Role
panels.description: Who led when. A switchover or failover shows as the green bar moving; gaps are scrapes that failed (the member or its Patroni was down).

panels.title: Patroni events
panels.description: Promotions, demotions, switchovers, failovers, rejoin/rewind lines from Patroni and Postgres on all members (Loki, app=patroni).

targets.expr: {app="patroni"} != `no action` |~ `(?i)promot|demot|switchover|failover|following a different leader|starting as a secondary|acquired (the )?leader|lost (the )?leader|released leader|leader key|reinitializ|pg_rewind|bootstrap|paused|resumed|maintenance mode`

panels.title: Replay lag (bytes behind the leader)
panels.description: Patroni's view, the one failover uses: past maximum_lag_on_failover (1 MiB) a replica can't become leader (alert PatroniReplicaLag).

targets.expr: scalar(max(patroni_xlog_location{job="patroni", scope="$scope"} and on (host) (patroni_primary{job="patroni", scope="$scope"} == 1))) - (patroni_xlog_replayed_location{job="patroni", scope="$scope"} and on (host) (patroni_replica{job="patroni", scope="$scope"} == 1))

panels.title: Replication lag (time)
panels.description: postgres_exporter: 0 when the replica has replayed everything it received, else the age of the last replayed transaction.

panels.title: WAL written / received
panels.description: WAL the leader generates and each replica receives; the lines should overlap.

panels.title: Streaming replication (leader's pg_stat_replication)
panels.description: The walsenders on the leader: one per replica, state streaming. Lag is the WAL not yet replayed.

targets.expr: max by (application_name, client_addr, state, slot_name) (pg_stat_replication_pg_wal_lsn_diff{job="postgres"} and on (host) (patroni_primary{job="patroni", scope="$scope"} == 1))

defaults.noValue: No replica connected to the leader

panels.title: WAL kept for replication slots
panels.description: WAL each member holds back for a slot. A slot whose member is gone keeps growing until the disk (42 GB root, data dir included) fills: Patroni drops a missing member's slot only once it leaves the cluster.

panels.title: Apps
panels.description: The apps that use the cluster: NetBox and dark-triage through their HTTP probes on the VIP, Grafana through its own /metrics (any Grafana up).

panels.title: Connections per database (all members)
panels.description: Backends per database across the members. grafana = Grafana (graf01/02), netbox = NetBox (netbox01/02 web + worker), triage = dark-triage (triage01/02). postgres: Patroni, postgres_exporter and replication.

panels.title: Connections by state
panels.description: 'idle in transaction' holds locks and blocks vacuum: an app that leaves transactions open shows here.

panels.title: Commits per second (leader)
panels.description: Transactions committed per app database on the leader (only it takes writes; replicas serve no reads here). grafana = Grafana (graf01/02), netbox = NetBox (netbox01/02 web + worker), triage = dark-triage (triage01/02).

panels.title: Rows written per second (leader)
panels.description: Inserted + updated + deleted rows per app database: who drives the WAL volume.

panels.title: Longest open transaction
panels.description: Age of the oldest open transaction per database and state, on any member. Long ones (minutes) hold back vacuum and replication cleanup.

panels.title: Database size (leader)
panels.description: grafana = Grafana (graf01/02), netbox = NetBox (netbox01/02 web + worker), triage = dark-triage (triage01/02).

panels.title: Database size
panels.description: Per app database on the leader (the replicas are byte-identical).

panels.title: Growth per day (6 h trend)
panels.description: Linear trend of each database's size, as bytes per day.

panels.title: pgBackRest backups
panels.description: pg-backup's result on each member that ran it (node_exporter textfile): the timer fires on all three, only the leader backs up. A member that led before shows its last run too.

defaults.noValue: No pgBackRest result for this stanza yet

panels.title: WAL segments archived to S3
panels.description: 16 MiB segments pushed by archive_command (pgBackRest). Failures: S3 unreachable (alert PostgresWALArchiveFailing).

panels.title: pg_wal size
panels.description: WAL on disk per member. Above max_wal_size: checkpoints can't recycle it (archiving stuck, or a slot holds it).

panels.title: Checkpoints
panels.description: Per hour. Requested checkpoints (WAL reached max_wal_size) instead of timed ones mean max_wal_size is too small for the write load. Replicas do restartpoints.

defaults.noValue: Needs postgres_exporter's stat_checkpointer collector (postgres.tf, not applied yet)

panels.title: Checkpoint write / sync time
panels.description: Share of time spent writing and fsyncing checkpoint buffers. Sync time follows Ceph RBD write latency.

defaults.noValue: Needs postgres_exporter's stat_checkpointer collector (postgres.tf, not applied yet)

panels.title: RGWs healthy behind haproxy
panels.description: pgBackRest reaches S3 through haproxy on 127.0.0.1:7443; 0 means archiving and backups fail (alert PostgresRGWBackendDown).

panels.title: etcd role
panels.description: Raft leader per member. Without quorum Patroni can't renew the leader key; failsafe_mode keeps the running leader as long as it can reach both replicas.

panels.title: WAL fsync p99 vs heartbeat
panels.description: etcd's data dir is on Ceph RBD, whose fsync p99 is 125-355 ms; heartbeat-interval 300 ms and election-timeout 3 s were raised for it (DT-017). fsyncs regularly above the heartbeat line bring the hourly re-elections back.

panels.title: Leader changes and failed proposals
panels.description: Per hour. Each member counts the same election once.

panels.title: Peer round trip p99
panels.description: Between the members over the Postgres HA VLAN.

panels.title: Patroni → etcd: key refreshed
panels.description: Since each Patroni last wrote its member key (every loop_wait = 10 s). At the ttl a leader that can't reach etcd loses the lock.

panels.title: DB size and proposals
panels.description: Patroni's keys are tiny; auto-compaction (1 h) keeps the db small. Commits/s is Patroni's write rate (member keys and the leader lock).

panels.title: Memory used
panels.description: 4 GiB VMs; shared_buffers is part of it, the rest is page cache.

panels.title: Disk busy and latency (vda, Ceph RBD)
panels.description: The data dir, pg_wal and etcd all sit on vda (Ceph RBD). Write await is what fsync waits for.

panels.title: Root FS used
panels.description: Postgres data, pg_wal and etcd live on /.

targets.expr: 1 - node_filesystem_avail_bytes{job="node", role="postgres", mountpoint="/"} / node_filesystem_size_bytes{job="node", role="postgres", mountpoint="/"}

panels.title: Postgres errors per member
panels.description: ERROR/FATAL/PANIC lines from Postgres (a failed query, a client that went away, ...).

panels.title: Patroni warnings and errors per member
panels.description: Patroni's own WARNING/ERROR lines: mostly etcd timeouts (watchprefix, read timed out).

panels.title: etcd warnings per member
panels.description: etcd logs JSON; slow fsyncs and apply requests show up as 'took too long'.
